SMTO-HTTP-0077 — Sign in to the service so SMTO can continue

GUID: 3d1fe9c1-336e-47b3-947b-4e7f8887e444
Slug: http-oauth-authorization-required
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • This service wants you to approve SMTO's access on its own sign-in page. The task is paused at this step until you finish.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the conversation, find the message Complete OAuth authorization to continue and select Open authorization page. The service only lets SMTO in after you approve access on its own page.
  2. Sign in with the account SMTO should use and approve the access it asks for. If a Device code is shown, select Copy device code and enter it on that page. The device code links your approval on that page to this waiting task.
  3. Come back to SMTO and wait a moment; the task continues on its own. SMTO notices the approval and carries on with the step that was waiting.

What success looks like

  • The sign-in message goes away and the task continues past this step.

If it still fails

  • If the sign-in page won't open or shows an error, select Stop in the sign-in message. Then select Copy error details and send them to the person who set up this connection. Don't type passwords or tokens into the conversation or a screenshot.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The OAuth provider requires an interactive authorization-code or device-code step before this HTTP connection can be used; the run waits on that authorization.

What this means

  • OAuth requires an authorization-code/device interaction and the private descriptor is returned through the existing human authorization boundary. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • OAuth requires an authorization-code/device interaction and the private descriptor is returned through the existing human authorization boundary.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the current owned authorization transaction, intended account and expiry; do not reuse another run's code.

How to fix it

  • OAuth2.prepare_session raised AuthInteraction and the run waits on http_oauth_requirement. Complete the flow at the presented authorization_url or verification_uri with the intended account, then confirm the connection's session is authenticated; if the flow cannot start, check authorization_endpoint, redirect_uri or device_authorization_endpoint in the saved profile.
  • Complete the displayed authorization flow for the intended provider account, then inspect connection status.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The supported authorization completes and the connection's current session is confirmed.

What not to do

  • Do not put credentials in task text, command arguments, screenshots or diagnostic reports.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
